result.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
result.summary: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction. Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates. Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking. We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Predictions improve when the model is told the opponent's type and parameter settings, but become less accurate when it must infer the opponent from history without this information. Training on examples that also omit these details reduces the gap, although improvements vary across opponents. Is this limitation specific to smaller open-weight models, or does it also appear in a frontier model? GPT-5.4 also benefits from correct opponent beliefs: supplying them improves its predictions and choices, whereas deeper explicit belief reports and self-generated memory do not consistently improve forecasting from interaction history. This contrast suggests that using useful belief information is easier than inferring it autonomously, even for a frontier model. Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出重复捉迷藏基准与诊断框架，通过实时交互、固定历史评估和受控信息干预，区分 LLM 智能体的适应性行为、对手动作预测与对递归信念的跟踪，并用监督微调与信息有无条件测试小模型和前沿模型的预测与决策表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属多智能体心智理论与信念状态研究，其「表现提升≠信念跟踪」的区分、以及提供或隐去对手信念/类型的干预设计，可能为 LVR 中判断 latent 状态是否被真正利用、区分行为捷径与内部状态推理提供问题表述与评价线索，可供核查。
